notes: -Wall is -Wwarn-lint plus -Wwarn-style and excludes some specialty warnings; -Wwarn-style lists DECLFILENAME, SYNCASYNCNET, UNDRIVEN, UNUSEDSIGNAL and the other style warnings; --lint-only checks and makes no other output; -Wno-<message> overrides lint_on; -Wno-fatal advice, --unused-regexp default *unused*; all on the Arguments page and as the document says.

Each warning the document lists was found in the Warnings page, with the fix it gives. A local run of verilator --lint-only -Wall 5.052 confirmed that a file with a mismatched name, an unused and an undriven signal, a width truncation, a latch, a blocking assignment in a clocked block, a delayed assignment in a combinational block, an incomplete, a casex and an overlapping case, an implicit net, a missing pin, an out-of-range select, SYNCASYNCNET and MULTIDRIVEN fails with the codes the document names, and that a misspelled metacomment is an error (BADVLTPRAGMA). BLKANDNBLK was not raised for a non-overlapping split of one vector in this version, as the page says since 5.038.

UNOPTFLAT: the document says it fails lint.run under -Wall, as an inference from the gate lines. On Verilator 5.052 with default flags the manual's own example, wire [2:0] x = {x[1:0], shift_in}, did not warn under --lint-only -Wall, because the DFG optimiser resolves it; with -fno-dfg the same file raises UNOPTFLAT under --lint-only. The gate passes no such flag, so the claim holds only where the optimiser leaves the loop. The sentence is an overstatement on 5.052 and is reported to the document's owner; it does not change a Knowledge reading of the rest.
